subject: Clarification: customer VPC isolation assumptions & security summary requested
messages:
From: Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@acme-inc.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-inc.com
Date: 2026-06-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: scope assumptions + redacted security summary for private deployment

Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — Acme's security team is finalizing our internal third‑party risk review and we need two things from Redwood for our planned Private deployment in our VPC:

1) A short, redacted summary of the most recent security assessment you ran that is relevant to customer-managed VPC deployments (we don't need full internal findings but want to see evidence of scope, high/medium findings, and remediation status).

2) A clear statement of your operational boundary assumptions for a Redwood Private deployment inside a customer VPC. Concretely: which network elements and services run in Acme's account/subnets versus Redwood-managed assets (control plane, telemetry, agent images, etc.), whether nodes ever receive inbound connections from the public internet, and what outbound egress destinations are required.

We're particularly worried about two things: (a) residual outbound connections from the runtime to third‑party telemetry or telemetry/CDN endpoints, and (b) whether your pen testing included exercises inside the customer's subnets (simulated attacker from a compromised subnet) or only tests of Redwood-managed infrastructure.

If you can share a redacted PDF and a short diagram of the boundary assumptions that would be ideal. If the full report is available under an NDA, we can sign — otherwise the redacted summary and attachments will suffice.

Can you also include current remediation status for any medium/high findings that might affect data isolation?

Thanks,

Tony Ruiz
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme Financial Technologies
security@acme-inc.com

---
Attachment: acme_request_20260630.eml (original request)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@acme-inc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope assumptions + redacted security summary for private deployment

Tony — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a redacted summary and a boundary diagram (see attachments). High level answers up front and then details below.

Short answers:
- We run the inference runtime (workers) inside customer-provided subnets when you choose the "Customer VPC" deployment model. Those worker instances are deployed into your subnets (no public inbound IPs by default).
- Redwood control plane (management/orchestration) runs in a Redwood-managed account unless you opt into our "private control-plane" option; control plane communications are mutually authenticated via mTLS and are restricted to specific egress ports.
- Persistent storage (KV caches, blobs) is configurable: by default caches are ephemeral in the runtime; persistent artifacts (optional: S3) are configured into customer buckets when requested. Keys remain customer-managed when KMS integration is enabled.
- Outbound connections: runtime may perform outbound calls for model downloads, package origins, and optionally for telemetry/reporting. Telemetry endpoints are documented and can be disabled per-contract.

What we attached: redwood_pt_summary_acme_vpc_20260629.pdf (redacted summary of our most recent independent assessment relevant to customer-VPC deployments) and a VPC boundary diagram (redwood_vpc_boundary_diagram.png). The PDF is sanitized to remove customer-identifying details and full exploitation steps — if you need the unredacted report we can provide it under a mutual NDA.

Scope clarification (what was/wasn't tested):
- Included in scope: the Redwood runtime image and its configuration when deployed into a customer VPC; privilege escalation attempts on the worker host; inbound port hardening; the bootstrap/call-home channel from worker -> Redwood control plane; image supply-chain checks for runtime artifacts.
- Excluded from scope: customer-managed services (your DBs, your VPN endpoints, other unrelated customer-managed compute), transit gateways outside the targeted subnets, and any managed services we did not replicate in our test harness (if you use a proprietary third-party gateway we recommend a joint validation).

Remediation status (summary):
- 2 medium findings (temporary credential rotation policy, and a misconfigured container capability) — both have been patched and redeployed as of 2026-06-20 (see the PDF for patched commit ids and CVE references).
- 1 low finding related to a non-default debug flag — mitigation scheduled for 2026-07-07 and will be included as a config rollup for customers.
- No open high-severity findings.

Evidence we can provide upon request (or via shared Drive link):
- Redacted report (attached)
- VPC boundary diagram (attached)
- Sample VPC flow logs and audit snapshots (we can push to your secure Drive folder)
- Signed test plan for the job we ran that specifically simulated a compromised customer subnet

Next steps: if you want the full report we can start the NDA and provide it within 48 hours of execution. Otherwise I'm happy to set a 30‑minute call with our security engineer (Karthik) and me to walk through the diagram and remediation notes. Proposed times: 2026‑07‑01 09:00 PDT or 2026‑07‑01 14:00 PDT.

Regards,

Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0193

Attachments: redwood_pt_summary_acme_vpc_20260629.pdf (redacted, high/med findings + remediation table); redwood_vpc_boundary_diagram.png (annotated)

From: Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@acme-inc.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-inc.com
Date: 2026-06-30T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope assumptions + redacted security summary for private deployment

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Soojin — the summary looks good. Two quick clarifications before we loop legal for an NDA:

1) For the remediation items you marked as "patched and redeployed": can you provide the CI/CD link or commit id and the timestamp for the production rollout? We need an auditable point-in-time indicator for our tracker.

2) Can you confirm whether any outbound connections are made to third-party telemetry/CDN domains that are not under Redwood's control (we prefer allow-listing to an internal Redwood domain where feasible).

3) For the simulated compromised subnet test: did your test harness exercise lateral movement against the customer's NAT/IGW, or were tests strictly limited to the worker hosts and their immediate neighbor subnets?

If you can drop those three items into a short follow-up email that should be enough for us to decide whether an NDA is required.

—Tony

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@acme-inc.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope assumptions + redacted security summary for private deployment

Tony — hi, Karthik from Redwood security here. Answers below with links to artifacts we've uploaded to the shared Drive link in my signature.

1) Rollout evidence: patched commits referenced in the PDF are 9f1d3b4 and 9f1d3c0; those were merged 2026-06-14 and the reconciler completed the rollout to the private-deploy test harness at 2026-06-20T03:10:00Z. CI runs and signed artifacts are in: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/patches/9f1d3b4-9f1d3c0 (redacted logs).

2) Outbound connections: by default the runtime performs outbound requests only for model retrieval (from Redwood artifact store) and image package verification. Telemetry is opt-in; if enabled telemetry endpoints are routed to telemetry.redwood.ai and are under Redwood's control. We do not call third‑party telemetry domains by default. Customers who enable optional analytics or remote-hosted model stores may introduce additional endpoints; those are documented and can be locked down by allow-listing.

3) Compromised subnet testing: for the customer-simulated run we exercised both: (a) host-level compromise on a worker instance and attempts at privilege escalation and local lateral movement inside the same subnet; and (b) attempts to reach customer-managed NAT/IGW resources from the compromised host to validate network ACL and routing restrictions. We did NOT perform an authenticated attempt against Acme-managed DBs or external VPN endpoints; those were explicitly out-of-scope and we documented them in the test plan.

Artifacts provided to Acme:
- VPC flow log extract (redacted) -> https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-vpc-diagram/flowlogs-redacted.csv
- Redacted audit log snapshot (worker auth & reconciler events) -> https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-vpc-diagram/audit-snapshot-20260620.json
- Signed redacted test plan (includes exact IP ranges exercised) -> https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-vpc-diagram/test-plan-signed.pdf

If you prefer, we can place these artifacts into an Acme-controlled S3 bucket with limited lifetime credentials. Let me know your preference and whether you want us to proceed with an NDA for the full report.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-vpc-diagram
